subject: Weekly MAP Checkpoint: Dedicated / Private Capacity Sizing — Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T09:00:00Z
Subject: Weekly MAP Checkpoint: Dedicated / Private Capacity Sizing — Acme Health

Hi Elena / Acme team —

Following up from our pilot evaluation kickoff, this is our weekly MAP checkpoint focused on dedicated/private capacity sizing. Attached is an updated MAP (MAP_AcmeHealth_v1.xlsx) and the Sizing CSV we discussed. High-level ask for today: align on GPU types, target regions, and throughput targets so we can lock the Dedicated configuration and provide a cost estimate by end of week.

Summary of current status (from our end):
- Pilot metrics: 95th p95 latency ~ 180ms (small-batch inference) on hosted M-Large.
- Eval throughput target: 40k tokens/min sustained during peak daytime window.
- Goal for Dedicated/Private: predictable 99th percentile latency < 250ms, support burst to 60k tokens/min.

Options we're proposing (see gpu_sizing_recommendations.csv):
1) 4 x A100 80GB in us-east-1 (best raw throughput, highest cost)
2) 8 x A10G in us-east-1 (cost-efficient for multi-stream workloads)
3) Hybrid: 2 x A100 80GB dedicated + autoscale to 4 x A10G for bursts (regional routing)

Questions for Acme:
- Do you require on-prem / VPC-only deployment for PHI workloads, or is VPC peering acceptable?
- Preferred primary region (us-east-1 vs us-west-2) for data residency?
- Which throughput profile matters most: sustained vs peak bursts?

Action items proposed for this week:
- Acme to confirm region and PHI restrictions (owner: Elena) — due Thu 2026-02-18
- Redwood SRE (Vivek) to run a simulated load test on the Hybrid option and share results — due Fri 2026-02-20
- Redwood to send cost estimate and SLA draft (owner: Marissa) — due Fri 2026-02-20

Attachments: MAP_AcmeHealth_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestones), gpu_sizing_recommendations.csv

Thanks — looking to keep momentum.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Elena Soto <elena.soto@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T11:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP Checkpoint: Dedicated / Private Capacity Sizing — Acme Health

Marissa / Elena —

Quick pass on sizing recommendations after an initial profiling run against Acme's sample workload (thanks Dev for the payload):
- Baseline inference shape: average input length ~ 320 tokens, average output ~ 120 tokens, 1.6 streams/sec per user session.
- Latency sensitivity: 95th p95 target <= 250ms suggests we should avoid very small GPU footprints.

Concrete recommendations:
- If Acme wants single-region lowest-latency (us-east-1): 3 x A100 80GB (reserved) gives headroom for sustained 45k tokens/min and consistent latency; add 2 x A10G as autoscale pool for burst to 70k.
- If cost-priority over headroom: 10 x A10G reserved with smarter routing and prefix caching — more complex but ~25% cost savings.
- For a private VPC appliance (on-prem style): we recommend 2 x H100 (if available locally) for best single-server density; otherwise 4 x A100 40GB. H100 procurement timing can add 6–8 weeks.

I'll run the Hybrid sim on a small cluster tomorrow and post numbers. Note: storage of KV caches will impact peak token costs; recommend we size ephemeral NVMe to 2TB per A100 instance in Dedicated.

I'll attach the raw profiling CSV in a follow-up.

-Vivek

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP Checkpoint: Dedicated / Private Capacity Sizing — Acme Health

Thanks Marissa/Vivek —

Responding to your questions: we need VPC-only deployment (no on-prem hardware for now) because of PHI controls; VPC peering is acceptable but traffic must remain in us-east-1 for primary processing. Our core requirement is consistent sustained throughput during business hours (08:00–20:00 ET) with ability to absorb 30–40% spikes. Peak bursts beyond that are lower priority.

Action from Acme:
- Confirmed region: us-east-1 (owner: Elena) — confirmed now.
- Procurement will review cost estimate once received (procurement@acmehealth.com).

One ask: can Redwood provide a short note on fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity is temporarily reduced (e.g., fall back to hosted with rate-limited throughput)? We need that in the MAP for procurement risk assessment.

Regards,
Elena Soto
Head of AI Platforms | Acme Health
elena.soto@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-16T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP Checkpoint: Dedicated / Private Capacity Sizing — Acme Health

Elena — thanks for the quick confirmation on region and PHI constraints. Per your request, adding a brief fallback note below (we will add to MAP_AcmeHealth_v1.xlsx and SLA draft):

Fallback behavior (summary):
- Primary: Dedicated pool in us-east-1 serving production traffic with reserved capacity (config TBD).
- If reserved capacity degrades (hardware maintenance / transient shortage), requests will be routed by policy to a compatible hosted model variant in the same region.
- During fallback, throughput will be rate-limited to a predefined safety window; Redwood will provide a circuit-breaker policy and a traffic-shaping rule (we'll propose defaults: 60% sustained throughput, 1.5x normal latency SLO).
- SLA credits will apply if fallback extends beyond agreed thresholds; details in SLA_draft_Acme_2026.pdf.

Proposed next steps and owners:
- Vivek: complete Hybrid sim and provide numbers (due Fri 2026-02-20).
- Marissa: share cost estimate and SLA draft (SLA_draft_Acme_2026.pdf) — sending by EOD Fri 2026-02-20.
- Elena: procurement review and initial feedback (procurement@acmehealth.com) — target Mon 2026-02-23.

I'll update the MAP file with the fallback language and include the hybrid vs A10G-only cost delta.

Best,
Marissa

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Weekly MAP Checkpoint: Dedicated / Private Capacity Sizing — Acme Health

Team —

Reviewed the notes. Approve proceeding with the Hybrid proposal as primary recommended configuration for the initial committed Dedicated offering: 2 x A100 80GB reserved + autoscale to 4 x A10G for burst. Finance will accept a short pilot pricing concession to close this by end of month; coordinate with Dylan to finalize the pilot discount and term.
